title: IoT and Blockchain Applications in Agriculture: A Systematic Review of Techniques, Effectiveness, and Challenges
content: Agriculture faces resource scarcity, climate variability and weak supply-chain transparency, and research on the Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain as responses is fragmented. We conducted a systematic review reported under PRISMA 2020 of 79 sources (2012–2026; 58 from an initial search and 21 from a targeted 2024–2026 update). Sources were separated into 45 reviews and surveys, used as related work, and 34 regular research papers, of which 27 technical studies were coded by technique, components and application domain. IoT-based approaches account for 52% of the technical studies, integrated IoT–blockchain approaches for 26% and blockchain-only approaches for 19%; the integrated share rose from 10% in the initial search to 26% after the update. Crop applications make up 41% of studies and livestock-only applications 15%. Reported benefits include better monitoring, input efficiency, traceability and data trust, but effectiveness metrics are heterogeneous. An analytical model of sensing load, ledger throughput, Byzantine fault tolerance and sharding explains why integration stresses throughput. Scalability, interoperability, cost and digital skills remain barriers; lightweight and sharded consensus and field-validated integrated systems are priority directions.
